strategy_summary:
Keppel Infrastructure Trust (KIT) has implemented a comprehensive decarbonization strategy centered on two key levers: energy optimization and expanding renewable energy exposure. The company has set concrete targets to achieve a 30% reduction in carbon emissions intensity by 2030 (measured against 2019 levels) and to establish a renewable energy portfolio comprising up to 25% of Assets Under Management (AUM) by 2030. In 2023, KIT demonstrated significant progress by reducing carbon emissions intensity by 36% from 2019 levels, exceeding its 2030 target, while increasing renewable energy exposure to 19% of AUM as of January 2024, up from 10% in 2022. The Trustee-Manager is also evaluating its carbon emissions strategy with the intention to set longer-term emissions reduction targets beyond 2030.

KIT is executing this strategy through several specific initiatives. The company made its first solar investment with a 45% stake acquisition in a German solar portfolio comprising over 60,000 photovoltaic systems, adding 585 MW of generation capacity and bringing KIT's total renewable generation capacity to approximately 1.3 GW. City Energy, a KIT subsidiary, is advancing hydrogen initiatives through a Joint Feasibility Study Agreement with Gentari to construct a pipeline from Malaysia to Singapore for hydrogen import, supporting Singapore's hydrogen economy development. Additionally, KIT is expanding its electrification efforts through Go by City Energy's exclusive rights to install EV charging services for 20,000 carpark lots and the proposed acquisition of Ventora, an Australian transportation business committed to converting 25% of its 900-bus fleet to electric by 2030. Energy efficiency measures include planned heat efficiency upgrades at Keppel Merlimau Cogen Plant and roof design improvements at SingSpring Desalination Plant to maximize natural daylight.

KIT supports its decarbonization strategy through robust governance and risk management frameworks. The company has fully adopted the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD) recommendations through a progressive implementation roadmap, conducting qualitative and quantitative scenario analyses to identify climate-related risks and opportunities. KIT utilizes climate scenario analysis to assess potential physical risks such as extreme precipitation and sea level rise, with specific business responses including regular assessment of mitigation options and infrastructure resilience reviews. The Trustee-Manager has also begun quantifying the financial impact of transition risks and is developing a comprehensive transition plan to enhance KIT's portfolio resilience against climate change impacts while maintaining strong financial performance.

Their approach is further strengthened by alignment with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals and the Science Based Targets Initiative, providing a credible framework for their climate action. strategy_summary:
Singtel's 2023 decarbonization strategy centers on a science-based approach aligned with the Paris Agreement's 1.5°C pathway, with an accelerated net-zero target of 2045. The company has structured its climate action around three key pillars: managing GHG emissions in line with climate goals, linking emissions to financing to drive behavioral change, and addressing physical climate risks through network adaptation. Singtel has refreshed its Science-Based Targets initiative (SBTi) commitments, bringing forward its net-zero goal from 2050 to 2045 and committing to a 42% reduction in absolute Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions by 2030 from 2015 baseline. The company completed a comprehensive review of its SBTi targets to ensure alignment with the 1.5°C scenario, which was submitted for validation.

The company implemented eight specific energy reduction initiatives in FY2023, including the installation of energy-efficient chiller systems across facilities (targeting units operating for 15+ years), replacement of aircraft warning lights with LED alternatives, and modernization of base stations to more energy-efficient 5G models. These initiatives collectively achieved estimated annual savings of 1,221.73 MWh and avoided 518.38 tCO2e of GHG emissions. Singtel also completed four solar energy generation projects totaling 1.38MWp across Singapore sites, with an annual generation capacity of 1,700MWh. The company secured renewable energy through multiple channels, including 30,000MWh of renewable energy power purchase agreements (PPAs) annually in Singapore and 296,000MWh of renewable-backed electricity in Australia from 2025-2029.

Supporting these operational efforts, Singtel established robust governance structures with board oversight of climate-related risks and opportunities. The company achieved ISO 14001 certification and was listed on the CDP Supplier Engagement Leaderboard for the first time. Singtel conducted TCFD scenario-based assessments to identify climate change risks and opportunities, and completed its first physical and transition climate risks TCFD climate scenario analysis for operations in northern NSW, Australia. The company also engaged with industry partners through the GSMA Climate Taskforce to develop sector-specific guidance on circular economy and mobile device environmental impacts, while contributing to standards development for e-waste recyclers in Singapore.

strategy_summary:
Polaris Renewable Energy’s 2023 decarbonization strategy centers on three interconnected pillars: emissions measurement and reduction, renewable energy-driven emissions avoidance, and climate resilience through structured risk assessment. The company prioritizes quantifying its carbon footprint to identify reduction opportunities, as evidenced by its 2022 baseline measurement for Nicaragua operations, which revealed 97.8% of emissions (scope 1) originated from geothermal energy generation and were compensated via UNFCCC-defined carbon credits. The remaining 2.2% of emissions—linked to fossil fuel consumption, energy use (scope 2), and operational activities like waste generation and business travel (scope 3)—are targeted for reduction through ongoing monitoring and process optimization. This measurement framework directly supports the company’s goal of assessing and reducing its carbon footprint while quantifying emissions avoided through its renewable energy projects.

To strengthen long-term resilience, Polaris has initiated a Climate Change Risk Assessment (CCRA) for its geothermal operations in Nicaragua’s San Jacinto community. Developed using Inter-American Development Bank methodologies, the CCRA evaluates climate-related hazards, identifies adaptation opportunities, and informs a Climate Risk Management Plan. This plan includes conceptual analysis, climate modeling, and strategic action plans spanning short-, medium-, and long-term horizons to address risks from natural and human-related climate impacts. By integrating climate risk management into operational governance, the company ensures alignment with regulatory frameworks and prioritizes tangible benefits for project personnel and surrounding communities.

ValueMax's strategy includes developing a comprehensive emissions reduction plan that identifies quick-deployment components requiring minimal capital investment. The company has established monitoring systems for energy and water usage intensity, with specific metrics tracking year-over-year improvements. The company continues to enhance its identification and assessment of climate-related risks across short, medium, and long-term horizons to inform strategic decision-making and maintain business resilience in the face of climate change.

strategy_summary:
VICOM's decarbonization strategy for 2023 focuses on two interconnected pillars: climate-friendly mobility and renewable energy adoption, with clear short-to-long-term timeframes aligned with Singapore Green Plan 2030. The company has established specific emissions reduction pathways modeled to align with the Science Based Target Initiative's 1.5°C scenario, validated in June 2022, demonstrating commitment to limiting global warming to 1.5°C above preindustrial levels. Their approach is structured around concrete implementation across three time horizons: short-term (up to 2030), medium-term (up to 2040), and long-term (up to 2050), with targets designed to ensure current ESG performance remains aligned with these goals.

In FY2023, VICOM has implemented tangible decarbonization initiatives, including the installation of 2,946 solar panels across six premises as a first step toward incorporating renewable energy into overall consumption. The company also installed 2 EV charging stations at its SETSCO office premises in Bukit Batok and acquired 2 EV vans. These actions support VICOM's concrete transition plan to progressively convert half of its existing ICE vehicle fleet to electric vehicles by 2030, with the aim of completing a full switch by 2040. This mobility transition is being executed in alignment with parent company ComfortDelGro's vehicle transition plan to maximize carbon emission reductions.

To strengthen its strategic approach, VICOM conducts 'what if' scenario analysis to assess potential financial impacts of carbon pricing schemes, determining that under a mitigated scenario, additional financial carbon costs would be 12% - 95% lower than in an unmitigated scenario across all timeframes. The company also continuously reviews internal processes and explores new solutions to help achieve its climate transition goals. These integrated initiatives demonstrate VICOM's commitment to advancing climate-friendly mobility while systematically reducing Scope 1 and 2 emissions through renewable energy adoption and strategic fleet transition.

strategy_summary:
The company’s 2023 decarbonization strategy centers on aligning with science-based climate targets and operationalizing a 1.5°C pathway across its value chain. As a Science Based Targets Initiative (SBTi) signatory, it maintains SBTi-validated targets (<2°C) since 2019 and committed to the SBTi Net Zero target in 2023, with annual progress reporting. The strategy prioritizes Scope 3 emissions, which account for over 90% of total GHG (83.01 million tCO₂e), through supply chain initiatives like the COP27-published roadmap to halt commodity-linked deforestation (palm, soy, cocoa) and participation in the COP28 Action Agenda on Regenerative Landscapes. Additionally, the company collaborates with global partnerships such as the First Movers Coalition for Food and the Sustainable Market Initiative’s Agribusiness Task Force to drive regenerative agriculture and blended finance frameworks for 1.5°C-aligned sector roadmaps.

Operationally, the strategy focuses on decarbonizing processing facilities through targeted technology adoption and energy transition. In partnership with Schneider Electric, a decarbonization roadmap was developed for processing operations, including the 713 KWp solar farm at a Nigerian rice mill (replacing natural gas), a waste heat recovery system at a Nigerian flour/pasta facility (utilizing generator waste heat for steam), and a 1.3 MW cogeneration plant in Nigeria using rice husks as feedstock. The company also replaced fuel-based forklifts with electric models at its Nigerian integrated feed and protein facility. Biomass and renewable energy adoption plays a critical role, with biomass accounting for 51% (11.2 million GJ) and renewables for 6% (1.4 million GJ) of total energy consumption in 2023.

Supporting these efforts are robust governance and verification mechanisms, including independent data verification by Manufacturing and Technical Services (MTS) teams and annual reporting to the Carbon Disclosure Project. The company also leverages scenario analyses (e.g., 'Business as Usual' and '1.5°C' scenarios) and institutionalizes climate risk management through its Integrated Risk and Assurance Framework (IRAF), with quarterly reviews by sustainability committees to ensure transparency and continuous improvement in managing climate-related risks and opportunities.

OCBC's decarbonization strategy for 2023 centers on three interconnected pillars: establishing science-based sectoral targets, developing innovative financial solutions, and implementing robust governance structures. The bank unveiled specific net-zero targets for six high-emission sectors (Power, Oil & Gas, Real Estate, Steel, Aviation, and Shipping) with quantifiable 2030 and 2050 reduction targets, aligning with their commitment to contribute to a net-zero ASEAN and Greater China by 2050. Their approach emphasizes client partnership, recognizing that financial institutions play a critical role in supporting the transition to a low-carbon economy through strategic advisory and ecosystem partnerships.

The bank implemented several concrete initiatives to advance decarbonization, including launching the pioneering OCBC 1.5°C loan, which incentivizes corporates to set carbon emissions reduction targets aligned with internationally recognized science-based pathways. They recorded $56 billion in sustainable finance commitments, surpassing their $50 billion target, with over 100 new sustainable finance transactions totaling $14 billion. OCBC achieved carbon neutrality for their operational emissions and developed sector-specific sustainability-linked financial products, such as the first sustainability-linked loan in the cement sector aligned with SBTi-validated decarbonization trajectories and Hong Kong's first sustainability-linked dual-currency fixed rate loan in hospitality.

To support implementation, OCBC established the Board Sustainability Committee (BSC) in 2023 to oversee the net-zero strategy and sector-specific decarbonization approaches, and appointed a Group Chief Sustainability Officer. They utilize metrics like the Alignment Delta (AD) to track progress in specific sectors, particularly in Real Estate where they demonstrated positive portfolio performance compared to reference pathways. The bank also expanded their SME Sustainable Finance Framework to Malaysia, Indonesia, and Hong Kong, and partnered with STACS to simplify carbon accounting for SMEs through the ESGpedia platform, enabling more businesses to participate in the decarbonization journey.

strategy_summary:
UOB's decarbonization strategy for 2023 centers on three integrated pillars: maintaining operational carbon neutrality, supporting client transitions through sustainable finance, and managing climate risks across its portfolio. The bank achieved operational carbon neutrality for its own footprint (Scope 1, 2, and 3 business air travel) in 2021 and has established a decarbonisation roadmap for its real estate portfolio through energy conservation measures, renewable energy procurement, and carbon offsets. Specific operational initiatives include implementing more energy-efficient LED lighting systems, smart building sensors to optimize energy use, and upgrading air conditioning systems across facilities. For international shipping activities, UOB has partnered with DHL since 2022 to reduce carbon footprint and in 2023 deepened this commitment by planning to decarbonize its value chain through sustainable aviation fuels via DHL's GoGreen Plus programme, set for implementation in 2024.

To support client decarbonization, UOB has built a $44.5 billion sustainable finance portfolio by the end of 2023, exceeding its target of $30 billion by 2025. The bank has developed five specific sustainable finance frameworks aligned with international standards: Sustainable Finance Framework for Green Building Developers and Owners, Smart City Sustainable Financing Framework, Green Financing Framework for Circular Economy, Sustainable Trade Finance Framework, and Transition Finance Framework. These frameworks support clients across various sectors in their transition to low-carbon economies. UOB implements strict portfolio screening policies, including exclusion of companies deriving ≥20% of revenue from thermal coal mining/power generation without transition plans, and limiting to 10% portfolio weight for companies with ≥20% coal revenue but with transition policies in place. The bank also developed a policy to exclude companies involved in controversial weapons production, manufacturing, sales, or brokerage.

The bank's decarbonization approach is supported by robust governance structures and capacity building. In 2023, UOB established a Sustainability Advisory Panel to provide external perspectives on sustainability strategy, targets, and initiatives. The bank implemented mandatory Sustainability 101 e-learning for all employees globally, with close to 100% of new employees completing the training by end of 2023. Sustainability metrics are integrated into the Group Balanced Scorecard and variable pay pool, with climate-related considerations forming part of the Group Risk Appetite Statement. UOB conducts climate scenario analysis using a methodology that assesses transition risk scenarios and physical risk scenarios to inform its risk management approach, and has committed to broadening physical risk assessments to strengthen climate scenario analysis and stress testing.

Sheffield Green Ltd.'s decarbonization strategy centers on a climate change transition plan that commits to reducing absolute Scope 2 GHG emissions by 12.8% by FY2035, with FY2023 serving as the baseline year. The climate change transition plan is specifically focused on two strategic levers of reduce and neutralise to achieve their emissions reduction targets.

They are also developing mechanisms to track other Scope 3 categories where relevant and practicable. The company does not make separate disclosure on direct GHG emissions (Scope 1) as they are not material to their operations, but commits to monitoring them for future disclosure when applicable. Progress updates and performance metrics will be provided in future sustainability reports as the plan is progressively implemented.

To support implementation, the company incorporates decarbonisation strategy and performance in their sustainability reporting, executes the decarbonisation strategy through planned initiatives, and conducts assurance on the reporting process and performance through internal reviews. strategy_summary:
Boustead Singapore's decarbonization strategy for 2023 centers on operational efficiency and circular economy solutions within its core business operations. The company has implemented 230 heat recovery systems through its subsidiary Boustead International Heaters (BIH), which generate 52.8 terawatt-hours of annual thermal energy recovery. These systems capture thermal energy from high-temperature turbine exhaust and flue gases generated by oil & gas processes, reducing thermal energy loss, emissions, and carbon footprint while potentially doubling the operational efficiency of gas-fired turbines. This initiative has already delivered significant environmental impact, equivalent to reducing 86.5 million barrels of oil consumption or saving approximately S$4.8 billion in industrial gas tariffs. Additionally, BIH has developed an innovative thermal treatment system that recycles end-of-life and hard-to-recycle plastic waste into chemical feedstock, directly contributing to a circular economy and reducing environmental impacts through waste valorization.

To support these operational initiatives, Boustead has established robust environmental governance frameworks across its operations. The company's largest subsidiary, Boustead Projects, has obtained ISO 14001:2015 certification for its Environmental Management System (EMS), which sets out specific environmental management enablers, commitments, targets, and responsibilities. The Quality, Environmental, Health and Safety (QEHS) Teams oversee environmental performance at all workplaces and project sites, ensuring daily compliance and continuous improvement. The company is also a voluntary participant in Singapore's Building & Construction Authority Green & Gracious Builder Scheme, having received the 'Excellent' award in 2018 for its environmental and sustainability practices.

Boustead's strategy extends to digital infrastructure solutions that support sustainable development. Through its Geospatial Division, the company implements digital infrastructure solutions and digital twins, including smart mapping and location analytics, to support the development of hard and soft infrastructure that underpins a smart and sustainable world. These technology-driven solutions help clients improve energy efficiency, reduce emissions, and enhance climate resilience while supporting socio-economic growth in both developed and emerging markets.

The company's decarbonization approach centers on integrating climate risk management into its enterprise risk management (ERM) framework, with a focus on transitioning to a low-carbon economy in alignment with the Paris Agreement. The strategy employs a structured process of identifying, assessing, and managing climate-related risks and opportunities, with particular emphasis on transition risks related to policy changes, technological shifts, and market dynamics. The organization has established a dedicated Climate Strategy Committee (CSC) that reports to the Board, which oversees the sustainability strategy and integrates ESG considerations into strategic decision-making processes including acquisitions, divestments, and capital expenditures. This governance structure ensures accountability and strategic alignment across the organization for climate-related initiatives.

The company is implementing specific financial mechanisms to support its decarbonization efforts, most notably a sustainability Linked Loan with Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation Limited. This innovative financial instrument uses reduced emissions intensity from construction activities as a Key Performance Indicator (KPI) to determine interest rate discounts, directly tying financial incentives to emission reduction performance. The organization is also conducting materiality analysis to prioritize climate-related factors based on financial impact and strategic importance, using a structured framework that includes assessing transition impacts through Paris-aligned scenarios (below 2°C) to evaluate potential risks and opportunities.

The company's approach includes identifying transition opportunities in innovation (low-carbon technologies and energy efficiency), financial instruments (green finance and bonds), and brand reputation enhancement. strategy_summary:
Meta's decarbonization strategy centers on a multi-pronged approach focused on renewable energy adoption, carbon removal, data center sustainability, and climate resilience. The company has made significant progress in renewable energy, with a portfolio exceeding 10,000 MW of contracted renewable energy projects, making it one of the largest corporate buyers globally. Meta partners with utilities to add renewable energy to their systems and develops green tariffs that enable facilities and other customers to pursue renewable energy projects. For emissions that cannot be eliminated through reduction efforts, Meta supports a diverse portfolio of natural and technological carbon removal projects that must demonstrate additionality, durability, support for local livelihoods, environmental benefits, and third-party verification.

To drive deeper emissions reductions, Meta has implemented Life Cycle Assessments for data center hardware and developed internal visualization tools to identify the highest carbon-emitting components. The company has built a comprehensive dataset containing embodied carbon estimates for hundreds of millions of components, achieving more than 90% coverage in 2022. This data enables value chain carbon reductions by helping Meta select lower-carbon options and engage suppliers. Meta also integrates climate risk and resilience assessments into key business decisions such as site selection and infrastructure development, and works with supply chain partners to identify and manage climate risks.

Supporting these initiatives, Meta collaborates extensively to scale solutions. The company announced a joint $925 million commitment with Stripe, Shopify, McKinsey Sustainability, and Alphabet to accelerate carbon removal technologies. Meta partners with the Business Alliance to Scale Climate Solutions and, through 1t.org, collaborates with the National Indian Carbon Coalition to support land restoration projects that center Indigenous leadership. The company aligns its emissions reduction targets with the Science Based Targets initiative and follows the GHG Protocol for emissions calculations, ensuring third-party verification of its environmental data.
